chapter_theme: A song at Kanagamalai (கநகமலை): the poet asks to give up the bewildering pleasure of women and to see Murugan's faces, shining like sun and moon, so that all sorrow leaves him and he bows at his feet.

618.reading: The poet asks whether he will give up the one thing he longs for on the wrong path, the world's pleasure that follows women and bewilders him until his mind aches as a fool's, and asks that, seeing Murugan's exalted faces shining as if sun and moon stood full together, all his inner sorrows go and he praise with love and bow at the pair of feet. The praise names the Shakti vel that made the demons fade, the clan mountains shake and the seas tremble, Murugan coming with jingling ornaments while Gauri fondles him, the kadamba-chested younger brother of the elephant-faced god, at Kanagagiri.
618.nuance: The cure asked for is a sight: பரிதி மதி நிறைய நின்றஃதென ஒளிரும் உனது படிவ முகம், the faces bright as sun and moon together. கருணை பொழி கிருபை முந்தப் பரிவினொடு கவுரி கொஞ்ச: the praise includes a tender scene of the mother fondling the child.
